hard_exclusions.material_strategic_transaction: Acquisition, disposal, merger, buyout or restructuring announcement that changes consolidated scope or announces a material strategic transaction
hard_exclusions.ceo_succession_or_material_workforce_red: Chief executive succession or material workforce reduction announcement
hard_exclusions.material_legal_or_regulatory_action: New material litigation, criminal plea, export restriction or regulatory action
hard_exclusions.unresolved_common_share_basis: Split, reverse split, spinoff or other price-basis event with unresolved common share basis
hard_exclusions.duplicate_preliminary_earnings_or_guidan: A separate preliminary earnings or guidance disclosure in the observation window that duplicates or supersedes the economic event
hard_exclusions.unresolved_source_or_material_scope: Unknown provenance or unresolved material comparability is a hard exclusion, per the registered source-quality freeze rule.

soft_caveats.routine_share_repurchase_authorization: Routine share-repurchase authorization announced in the observation window
soft_caveats.routine_dividend_initiation_or_change: Routine dividend initiation or change announced in the observation window
soft_caveats.minor_board_or_officer_appointment: Minor board or officer appointment announced in the observation window, excluding chief executive succession

No new registered mask identified in the reviewed current packet.

Its 39-cent dividend matches the immediately preceding quarter; the 15% wording compares to 2023, not a new sequential increase. Alpine was acquired May 20 between the May 6 numeric prior and August 1 current range. June 27 updates acquisition expense accounting but does not explicitly reaffirm or reconcile consolidated revenue-guidance scope. Reviewed original sources do not establish comparable old/new consolidation basis; withhold under the fixed scope rule.

Both outlooks are consolidated FY2024 revenue. The current release increases an accrual for an already ongoing royalty-contract litigation matter relating to 2004-2017 and describes its prior established accrual. An updated earnings accrual does not itself establish a newly filed material lawsuit or new regulatory action under the fixed taxonomy. No additional registered in-window catalyst identified.

The August 6 original packet describes an AMG 193 FDA orphan designation in August without an exact earlier first-public date. This designation alone is not treated as a proven material approval or adverse regulatory action: both first-public timing and potential materiality of the new oncology-program regulatory disclosure remain unresolved. The source is conservatively withheld under the existing unresolved-provenance rule. Older approvals and the July TEZSPIRE designation do not independently create a new in-window mask.

Original issuer announcements precede the current release, but reviewed sources do not reconcile old/new consolidated guidance to a common basis. The August 7 amendment changes non-GAAP EPS only, repeats the revenue range, and was published after the August 7 feature cutoff.

The dated consolidated USD annual ranges refer to the same FY2024 and no newer numerical annual outlook or new registered catalyst was identified in the reviewed current-report chronology. Quarterly ranges and performance highlights do not replace the annual prior.

The same FY2024 annual scope is therefore established in both original releases. The Ansys transaction was announced in January and remains expected to close in 2025; July 12 regulatory notification neither closes it nor changes the FY2024 revenue scope. Actual FY2024 end is November 2, as stated in both releases; October 31 is presentation shorthand.

July 19 outage and subsequent July 22 filing precede the August observation window. The July filing does not replace the June annual numeric outlook. The current revenue update includes customer incentives; no new registered in-window acquisition, CEO change or litigation announcement was identified in the reviewed current packet.

Datum360 was acquired June 24, after the June 11 prior outlook and before the August update. The reviewed original outlooks do not explicitly reconcile the old and new consolidated revenue basis. This is an unresolved prior/current scope failure, not a new transaction in the shorter overnight catalyst window.

evidence.title: FDA pushes Lumakras colorectal cancer decision to early 2025
evidence.verification: Public primary-page extraction read through web tool; original reporter explicitly identifies an Amgen spokesperson confirming the review extension directly to FirstWord. Direct Python HTML retrieval failed expired TLS certificate; no certificate bypass or claim to original HTML-byte archival.
evidence.representation: web-tool primary-page extraction, not original HTML bytes

events.rationale: The current packet repeats the LUMAKRAS PDUFA extension from October 17 to January 17. FirstWord published its own original dated report October 18, explicitly identifying an Amgen spokesperson confirming the extension directly to FirstWord. This provides primary reporting before the October 30 regular-close anchor. Other product approvals in the packet occurred in earlier months. No new registered in-window mask identified in the reviewed chronology.

The latest active prior is the issuer August 27, 08:00 EDT completion release, which explicitly updates annual revenue to $19.5-19.8 billion including Belcan. October narrows it to $19.7-19.8 billion on the same consolidation basis. The original HTML timestamp plus one-minute buffer supplies availability; no SEC acceptance is fabricated.

evidence.finding: References August 6 guidance midpoint; no replacement annual USD range located.

events.rationale: Both outlooks are consolidated FY2024 revenue. October repeats the litigation accrual disclosed in August. The August 15 investor presentation labels its 2024E charts as based on the August 6 outlook rather than supplying a replacement numeric range.

December 2 discloses incumbent CFO retirement and a search, but no successor or interim appointment, so the fixed appointment caveat is not expanded to a retirement. December 4 earnings announces CFO departure and a search, without a replacement appointment; that is outside the fixed appointment caveat. The second December 4 8-K was accepted after the feature cutoff and is not backdated.

Reviewed originals do not explicitly establish comparable old/new revenue-guidance scope. The same release newly announces an additional $1 billion repurchase authorization approved December 3.

The December 9 release names Serge Tanjga as prospective interim CFO following the announced January 31 departure of the COO/CFO. This is a non-CEO officer appointment in the observation window. The October 16 convertible-note redemption notice and November bylaws amendment do not replace the annual revenue outlook.
